summary.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q2 FY27 total income rose 14% YoY to INR2,125 crore, a record, with EBITDA up 4% to INR270 crore and margin down to 12.7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 set a record quarterly total income of INR2,125 crore (up 14% YoY), with revenue from operations at INR2,075 crore (up 13%). Consolidated EBITDA rose 4% YoY to INR270 crore, but margin fell about 120 bps to 12.7% on freight, wool and cotton costs and higher brand spend ahead of the festive season. The company ended with a net cash surplus of INR69 crore versus a net debt of INR246 crore a year earlier, and working capital days fell to 82 from 105. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, mid-to-high double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 crore-plus net cash and double-digit PBT growth, with H2 expected to carry the year.

segments.name: Branded Textile
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR971 crore (+7% YoY); H1 INR1,650 crore (+3%). Segment EBITDA INR188 crore at 19.3% margin, helped by mix shift to pure wool and poly-wool blends; up 42% QoQ.

segments.name: Branded Apparel
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR559 crore (+20% YoY), highest ever quarterly; H1 INR908 crore (+14%). Segment EBITDA INR49 crore (+20%), margin stable at 8.8%, with casual brands ColorPlus and Parx leading.

segments.name: Garmenting (exports)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR339 crore (+26% YoY); H1 INR635 crore (+36%). EBITDA INR25 crore (+75%), margin 7.4% (+207 bps).

segments.name: High Value Cotton Shirting
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR222 crore (+5% YoY); EBITDA INR21 crore, margin 9.5%, pressured by raw material costs (cotton and flax) partly offset by higher ASPs. H1 revenue flat.

segments.name: Emerging Businesses
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR100 crore (+15% YoY), first time above INR100 crore; H1 INR179 crore. EBITDA negative INR23 crore in Q2; H1 losses reported as roughly doubled on analyst question.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: double-digit top-line growth, mid-to-high double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 crore-plus net cash/FCFF, and PBT at least double-digit higher (about INR220-225 crore).
Management expects H2 revenue growth above 10%, taking full-year growth above 10%, with H2 EBITDA margin likely above 12.7%.
FY27 capex about INR200 crore (some sources cited INR200-250 crore); net cash generation stated after this capex. FY28 budget not finalised.
Store count: 1,634 at Sep 2026 vs 1,653 at FY26 end; year-end target 1,665-1,670 (about +20 net), with H2 net additions of about 35-36 stores, mix of FOFO and COCO.
Branded Apparel margin guided to double-digit plus in a couple of years; Ethnix breakeven in 18-24 months; Home breakeven-plus by end FY27; Innerwear breakeven at year-end, real breakeven next year.
capex_capacity: Garmenting: Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) fifth plant expanded from 3 lines to 10 lines; over INR70 crore of capex going to Hindupur. Three lines are live; fourth line expected live Nov-Dec 2026, one line roughly every 3 months, all 10 lines in about 18-21 months.
Garmenting peak capacity about 10 million units after expansion; existing plants run at 90%+ utilisation; Ethiopia plant running at full capacity.
Capex also covers mill machinery upgrades, worker safety, ESG upgrades, COCO stores and SAP S/4HANA (textile and B2C go-live from 1 November 2026).
Pending FY27 capex of about INR200 crore; FY28 budget not yet finalised.
demand_pricing: Festive timing: Diwali on 8-9 November 2026 vs 22-23 October 2025, so primary loading partly shifted into Q3; management says Q2 loading was about half of last year's full loading.
Like-to-like store growth in double digits; Dussehra minus 45 days LFL +14%; Diwali minus 30 days offtake up about 20-23% YoY.
Casual brands (ColorPlus, Parx) grew at high double digits in Q2.
Garmenting order book: factories full till end January/mid-February 2027, booking end-February; Europe H1 up 30% YoY, Q2 up 50%; UK improving.
B2B pricing: management said only about 50-60% of raw material inflation can be passed on in high value shirting; newer orders priced higher.
Marriage dates strong from 15 November to 15 December and from mid-January to April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is Branded Apparel's strong growth driven by channel stocking from the festive shift or by secondary sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Diwali timing moved about 20-25 days; Q2 had only partial primary loading, yet Branded Apparel grew 20%, backed by secondary offtake and like-to-like store growth in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How will Branded Apparel margins move, and what is the medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin of 8.8% held despite higher marketing and raw material costs; management expects improvement from fresh pricing and scale, guiding to double-digit-plus margin in a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 deliver the FY27 guidance given H1 revenue up about 10% and EBITDA up mid-single digit?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 is seasonally larger (about 57-58% of revenue); with Diwali in November, management expects H2 revenue growth above 10% and H2 EBITDA margin above 12.7%, with cost-saving initiatives and full price pass-through in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow trajectory and why is H1 operating cash flow weak?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weak; net cash was INR69 crore vs minus INR246 crore a year ago. Management expects year-end cash of INR300 crore-plus vs INR179 crore last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 21% and what is brand spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand spend rose to INR116 crore from INR98 crore (+18%), 7.2% of B2C sales vs 6.8%; salaries rose about INR20 crore. Higher brand spend is budgeted to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did High Value Cotton Shirting margin compress, and when does it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton and flax costs stayed high, and B2B orders were booked earlier at lower prices; flax prices are stabilising and newer orders carry better prices, so H2 margin is expected to be better, with EBITDA margin double-digit-plus by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital discrepancy between balance sheet and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO explained that unutilised GST credits and other current assets/liabilities explain the gap; the days metric fell to 82 from 105, and management expects below 70 days at year end.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (crude at USD105-110/bbl, wool at multi-year highs, cotton and flax elevated) with partial pass-through in B2B lines.
Rupee near 94-95/USD; US tariff uncertainty; UK/EU FTA signing expected December 2026 and not yet implemented, so EU shipments depend on it.
Domestic demand risk from inflation, repo rate hike of 25 bps to 5.50%, weak monsoon, and election outcome in a large foreign country on 3 November.
Emerging Businesses losses (Q2 EBITDA negative INR23 crore); Ethnix breakeven 18-24 months away; Innerwear sleepwear run-off.
Working capital and H1 cash flow seasonality; store additions skewed to H2; Hindupur ramp-up efficiency lags line commissioning.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H2 and FY27 targets, backed by order book and Diwali/marriage-date visibility, but cautious on macro risks such as inflation, rates, and geopolitics. Management was candid that B2B margins are under pressure and that H1 cash flow is seasonally weak.

So chances are that we will do much better than 12.7% in EBITDA in H2.
So there is cautious optimism is what I'll say.
